0.label: esu_figure_with_long_cap_blowing_pipe
0.description: The whole drawing: a figure in profile, knees bent in a half-squat on a block, with a long cap falling down behind the head, bangles at wrist, waist and ankle, holding a long pipe or horn to the mouth that ends in a flared, knobbed bowl.
0.iconography: Captioned 'Edschu-Darstellung' — Ẹ̀ṣù, the messenger and trickster. The long hanging cap or hair-lock is his standard attribute; he is often shown with a pipe, flute or whistle. The same Ẹ̀ṣù whose face heads every Ifá tray.

panel.title: Drawing of Ẹ̀ṣù from a carved door: half-squatting figure with long cap and pipe
panel.object_type: archive sheet: outline drawing of one figure from a carved door
panel.summary: An outline drawing of a single figure copied from a carved door, captioned in German 'Representation of Edschu [Ẹ̀ṣù] on a carved door, Yoruba 3'. He half-squats with a long cap hanging behind his head and holds a long pipe or horn to his mouth.

register_readings.reading: One figure: Ẹ̀ṣù with cap, bangles and pipe.

panel.composition: A single figure lifted from a door register and drawn large on its own.
panel.narrative: The only named deity in the drawings. It shows that the doors, as well as the trays, carried Ẹ̀ṣù — the go-between who carries messages and offerings — so the door panels are not only chronicles of kings and wars but also include the figures who guard crossings and thresholds, which is exactly where a door stands.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral for 'chronicle'; a reminder that door panels mix ritual figures with historical ones.
cross_panel_links: Ẹ̀ṣù faces head the Ifá trays (e.g. FoA_04-5580, KBA_17556).
uncertainties: The object in his mouth could be a pipe, a horn or a whistle.
The pencil note below the caption is only partly legible ('…stellung von Türen').
